text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000203 bills 99215 far above expectation in every complexity tier, including patients with no chronic conditions, while the small chart sample neither confirms nor clears the pattern.","leaning":"pattern_consistent_with_upcoding","interpretation":"The excess is not explained by a sicker panel: 99215 share runs several times the all-provider share in every complexity stratum, and the gap is widest in relative terms among 0–1 condition patients. The sampled low-complexity 99215 claims carry routine diagnoses such as follow-up (Z09 on C0097073, C0097281, C0097690), abdominal pain (R10.9 on C0097398, C0097548) and UTI (N39.0 on C0097738, C0097800), which would rarely need high-complexity decision-making. The documentation cuts the other way but is too thin to judge. Only 11 documented 99215 claims came back, and their unsupported rate is close to the comparison rate, with several charts (e.g., C0097549, C0097581) recording high MDM and over 45 minutes. Those notes may not be reliable, though: nearly a third of returned notes look duplicated, no audit trail was received, and the data-reviewed mismatch on claims without lab lines is weak evidence that notes may be inflated to match the billed level. A reviewer should first request charts and audit trails for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed in the packet, checking whether the notes are cloned and whether the claimed data review matches what was actually ordered."}
